{{Short description|European academic organization}}
The '''European Mathematical Psychology Group''' ('''EMPG''') is an informal association of scientists in [[mathematical psychology]]. The group was founded in 1971 in Paris; it has not been formally organized as a society, although has been described as the "European branch" of the [[Society for Mathematical Psychology]].<ref>{{citation|title=The Corsini Encyclopedia of Psychology, Volume 3|first1=Irving B.|last1=Weiner|first2=W. Edward|last2=Craighead|edition=4th|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2010|isbn=9780470170274|page=972|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hhGdag3Wf-YC&pg=PA972}}.</ref> It holds a meeting each year in a European city, and beginning at the 23rd meeting, has published a [[proceedings]] from that meeting as an edited volume.<ref>{{citation|title=Recent Progress in Mathematical Psychology|editor1-first=Cornelia E.|editor1-last=Dowling|editor2-first=Fred S.|editor2-last=Roberts|editor2-link=Fred S. Roberts|editor3-first=Peter|editor3-last=Theuns|publisher=Psychology Press|year=1998|isbn=9780805819755|page=x|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xpsIC9M_LSUC&pg=PR10}}.</ref> As of 2001, there were approximately 100 attendees.<ref>{{citation|title=International Encyclopedia of the Social and Behavioral Sciences, Vol. 1|editor1-first=Neil J.|editor1-last=Smelser|editor2-first=Paul B.|editor2-last=Baltes|publisher=Elsevier|year=2001|isbn=9780080430768|page=9411}}.</ref>
